name: Dried fruit
anchor: Per-produce-class sovereign maximum levels for lead and cadmium (EU Reg. 2023/915 and Switzerland VHK 817.022.15; Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2; AU-NZ Schedule 19; MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019; Israel MOH FCS-2016), nickel under EU Reg. 2024/1987, total and inorganic arsenic under MERCOSUR and Israel MOH FCS-2016, and total mercury under Hong Kong Cap. 132V and Israel MOH FCS-2016.
native_basis_label: dried fruit as offered to the consumer, dry as-sold basis, no reconstitution conversion applied
scope_note: Sun-dried, tunnel-dried, osmotically dried, freeze-dried and vacuum-dried whole or cut fruit sold as such: raisins and sultanas, prunes, dried apricots, figs, dates, dried apples, dried mango and papaya, dried cranberries and cherries, and freeze-dried fruit pieces. Water content is roughly 15 to 25 percent against 80 to 90 percent for the fresh commodity, so a fresh wet-weight maximum level is between four and six times stricter than its own intent when applied to this row at face value. THE BASIS IS A CONTROLLING FACT FOR THIS ROW, BUT IT IS NOT THE ONLY ONE. Only maximum levels expressed on an as-offered or as-placed-on-market basis are named, enforced by the basis_guard; that admits both an instrument's express dried-commodity rows (Israel's category 3.1 for mercury and arsenic, MERCOSUR's dried-fruits rows for lead and total arsenic) AND an instrument's residual rows whose scope reaches the dried product on that same as-placed-on-market basis, which is how Israel's residual fruits-and-vegetables rows bind the lead and cadmium cells: Israel writes no dried-fruit carve-out in its lead or cadmium tables, so no basis conversion is involved and the residual row governs the dry product as sold. AU-NZ Schedule 19 is expressly excluded, because Schedule 19 calculates dried and dehydrated foods on the pre-drying basis and its fruit lead maximum level of 100 ug/kg is therefore a fresh-equivalent number rather than a dry as-sold number; the row's binding lead value of 100 ug/kg is numerically identical but comes from Israel MOH FCS-2016 on the as-placed-on-market basis, where no conversion is required. OUT OF SCOPE: dried leafy vegetables, dried herbs and dried spices (Category 34); dried mushrooms (Category 29); fruit leathers, strips, purees, gummies and other manufactured fruit confections (fruit-snacks row); dried pulses, nuts and seeds (Categories 27 and 28); products marketed for ages 0 to 5 (Category 1).
basis_guard: product as offered to consumer|product as placed on market
basis_guard_note: This row is a concentrated product in a dry or as-offered basis, so the guard admits only maximum levels expressed for the product as offered to the consumer or as placed on the market and rejects every fresh wet-weight and portion-ordinarily-consumed maximum level. That is deliberate: applying a fresh wet-weight value at face value to a dried product would silently mix bases, and converting between them would require an invented reconstitution factor, which Method v2.0 confines to infant formula.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only; the strictest applicable sovereign maximum level for the row's product form in the row's native basis, a disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated, a substantiated not-material determination, or a control; never occurrence-derived)

Pb.basis: dried fruit as offered to the consumer (dry as-sold)
Pb.label: Israel MOH FCS-2016 lead category 3 (fruits and vegetables except listed categories, 100 ug/kg, product as placed on market) is the strictest sovereign lead maximum level that reaches dried fruit in this row's own dry as-sold basis; MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 write an express dried-fruits lead row at 800 ug/kg, which is named so the government-written dried-fruit split stays visible.

Cd.basis: dried fruit as offered to the consumer (dry as-sold)
Cd.label: read-across from the GB 2762-2025 fresh-fruit cadmium maximum level (50 ug/kg) applied to the dried product as sold; drying concentrates the fruit, so the fresh-fruit level is at least as protective on the dried basis

tAs.basis: dried fruit as offered to the consumer (dry as-sold)
tAs.label: MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 set total arsenic for dried fruits at 800 ug/kg; Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 3.1 sets 5000 ug/kg for dried fruits and vegetables.
tAs.substantiation: R1 direct maximum levels for the dried commodity on the dry as-sold basis. MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 write an express dried-fruits total-arsenic row at 800 ug/kg and bind this cell; Israel's express dried category 3.1 at 5000 ug/kg is named and is looser. Israel's residual fruits-and-vegetables total-arsenic row (1000 ug/kg) is not the applicable Israeli category here, for the same reason as the inorganic-arsenic cell: Israel writes an express dried category for arsenic. It is looser than the binding value in any event. The inorganic-arsenic species limit for this row (300 ug/kg) is far stricter and is the operative arsenic constraint; total arsenic is reported for its own sake and is never satisfied by the species cell.

iAs.rationale: No in-force sovereign or general-food iAs maximum level applies to this product on the dietary-content basis after the supersession of regulations/israel-moh-fcs-2016-heavy-metals-tin-food-guidelines; the species is bounded by its parent total (tAs) per the certification-readiness ruling (species ≤ total).

tHg.basis: dried fruit as offered to the consumer (dry as-sold)
tHg.label: Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 3.1 sets total mercury for dried fruits and vegetables at 150 ug/kg, the only sovereign total-mercury maximum level written for a dried produce commodity.

MeHg.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a methylmercury maximum level for this product form, and no not-material determination is supportable for it: the routed corpus quantifies methylmercury in edible plant and fungal tissue (wang2021-houttuynia-mercury-china measured methylmercury in the leaf and root tissue of an edible leafy vegetable at an LOD of 0.002 ug/kg; stasinos2014-heavy-metals-tubers-review in root and tuber tissue; asensio2023-madrid-mushrooms-mercury), so the species is not absent from produce and the biological premise of a not-material determination is rebutted inside this very category. This row is the concentrated form of the fresh commodity, whose own methylmercury cell is held under the same control; a concentrated derivative is never granted a weaker determination than the fresh row it derives from. Methylmercury is therefore held under mandatory analytical control rather than recorded not-material, and it remains bounded by identity below the published total-mercury ceiling for this row (Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 3.1, 150 ug/kg); methylmercury cannot exceed total mercury. No methylmercury ceiling is invented.
MeHg.reference_method: Methylmercury by GC-ICP-MS or EN 16801, required only on a lot whose total mercury reaches 60 percent of the published total-mercury ceiling; any quantifiable methylmercury on such a lot is investigated and the lot is held pending root-cause analysis.

Ni.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a nickel maximum level for fruit in any form, dried or fresh. EU Reg. 2024/1987 enumerates vegetable, cereal, pulse, nut, seed, cocoa, seaweed and juice classes and sets no fruit maximum level at all, and the Swiss VHK nickel rows mirror it. There is therefore no same-commodity value to read across from, and a vegetable wet-weight nickel maximum level could not be carried into this row's dry as-sold basis in any event. HMTc publishes no nickel number for dried fruit.
Ni.reference_method: Total nickel by ICP-MS on every lot. Investigate any result that is an outlier against the applicant's own dried-fruit lot history, with attention to stainless-steel dicing and dehydrator contact, and record the drying ratio so results can be compared on a fresh-equivalent basis for surveillance.

Sn.rationale: Every tin maximum level in the register is scoped to canned product: EU Reg. 2023/915 sets 200000 ug/kg for canned foods and 100000 ug/kg for canned beverages, Codex CXS 193-1995 and AU-NZ Schedule 19 set 250000 ug/kg for canned foods, and Hong Kong Cap. 132V sets 250000 ug/kg for canned food other than canned beverages. Those limits regulate one contamination pathway, dissolution of tin from tinplate into the packed food. This row is not packed in tinplate, so the pathway that every sovereign tin limit addresses is physically absent and any tin present is dietary background rather than packaging migration. The EU tin maximum levels expressly exclude canned dried and canned powdered products from their own scope, which is the regulator's own recognition that tin dissolution from tinplate is a wet-pack phenomenon; even a canned dried fruit therefore falls outside every sovereign tin maximum level. Hermetically sealed tinplate presentations of this commodity route to the canned-foods row in Category 7 and carry the canned-foods tin maximum level there.
Sn.reference_method: Total tin by ICP-MS on every lot as part of the mandatory eight-totals panel; a result above 50 ug/kg is investigated for a metal-contact source in harvest, wash, transport or packing before the lot is released.
Sn.regulatory_basis: No jurisdiction sets a tin maximum level for non-canned produce; all tin maximum levels in the register are conditioned on a canned (tinplate) presentation, and the EU rows expressly exclude canned dried and canned powdered products from even that scope.
Sn.jurisdictions_checked: EU Reg. 2023/915; EU Reg. 2024/1987 (nickel); Switzerland VHK 817.022.15 (2026 metal/metalloid annex); Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule; AU-NZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19; MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019; Israel MOH FCS-2016; Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (21 CFR, action levels)

Al.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets an aluminium contaminant maximum level for any fruit, vegetable or produce form in any jurisdiction. The register's aluminium limits are drinking-water and bottled-water parameters, infant-formula maximum levels, a food-contact plastics specific migration limit, toy migration limits, and permitted-additive levels for baked and starch foods; none of them regulates aluminium as a contaminant of produce. Aluminium is also the third most abundant element in the earth's crust and appears in produce largely as soil-derived and root-associated mineral content rather than as process contamination, so no near-neighbour read-across is supportable either. Under the government-limit-only method HMTc publishes no standalone aluminium number for this row.
Al.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on every lot, reported to the applicant. Document any aluminium-containing processing aid, packaging contact or anti-caking agent, comply with the additive rules of every market of sale, and investigate any result that is an outlier against the applicant's own lot history.

Cr.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a total-chromium maximum level for this product form. The only dietary total-chromium maximum levels in the register are Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 7 for vegetables (500 ug/kg) and pulses, cereals, meat, fish and dairy powder rows under the same item, plus drinking-water and color-additive specifications. The Hong Kong vegetable row does not reach fruit, no jurisdiction writes a total-chromium maximum level for fruit, and a wet-weight vegetable value could not be carried into this row's dry as-sold basis. Under the government-limit-only method HMTc publishes no standalone total-chromium number for this row; total chromium is screened on every lot and hexavalent chromium is controlled by reflex speciation.
Cr.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every lot; investigate any elevated result against soil, irrigation water and processing-equipment provenance and reflex-speciate per the Cr-VI control.

Cr-VI.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum level for any solid food in any jurisdiction: the register's only ingested Cr(VI) parameters are drinking-water maxima (Australia NHMRC 2025, 50 ug/L; California SWRCB, 10 ug/L), which are water-basis parameters that do not reach a solid produce row and whose issuers are not admitted to this category's credible set as food regulators, and every other Cr(VI) row in the register is an article or material limit. This row also has no published total-chromium parent to bound the species against: the only dietary total-chromium maximum level in the register from a regulator in this category's admitted credible set, Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 7, is scoped to vegetables and does not reach this product form (the register's remaining dietary total-chromium rows are Chinese GB 2762 milk and milk-powder rows, a different commodity from a regulator outside the admitted set). With neither a species limit nor a published parent, HMTc publishes no hexavalent-chromium number and controls the species by mandatory reflex speciation.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every lot. Any total-chromium result at or above 100 ug/kg triggers Cr(VI) speciation by EN 15192 or EPA 6800 IC-ICP-MS isotope dilution; any quantifiable Cr(VI) at LOQ fails the lot and the lot is held pending root-cause analysis.
Cr-VI.bounded_by: Cr (total chromium, itself a control for this row)
